title: A novel RNA-binding activity of ECD contributes to U5 snRNP stability and pre-mRNA splicing.

verified.what_i_actually_checked: Downloaded and parsed 3 of the 4 processed files in GEO (Gene Expression Omnibus) series GSE285409 from the NCBI FTP site: IDRpeaks.bed.gz = 3,360 ECD binding peaks, 6 headerless columns (chromosome, start, end, two numeric scores, strand), 0 duplicate coordinates, peak width median 70 bases, 23 chromosomes with 29-358 peaks each; deseqresults...Total.txt.gz = 60,580 genes with baseMean, log2FoldChange, lfcSE, stat, pvalue, padj (22,488 rows have no fold change, 30,403 no adjusted p-value); gene_count_matrix...csv.gz = 60,580 genes x 6 RNA-seq samples (3 ECD-depleted, 3 control), library sizes 56-76 million reads, 18,742 genes with >=10 reads in all 6. I recomputed the paper's headline count: adjusted p < 0.05 and >2-fold gives exactly 3,452 genes, 1,317 down and 2,135 up.
verified.what_came_from_paper_text_only: That peaks were called with CLIPper on hg38 and filtered by IDR (irreproducible discovery rate) from 2 eCLIP replicates; that the de novo motif search (HOMER) found a purine-rich exonic splicing enhancer motif in 35% of peaks; that 5,070 differential splicing events in 2,595 genes were found with rMATS-turbo (that table is NOT in the deposit); that peaks were compared with 149 other RNA-binding proteins. The 38 MB log2 IP-versus-input signal track (bigWig) was listed in the FTP directory but not opened. Europe PMC's supplementary-file listing timed out twice, so the supplement is not retrievable; only Supplementary Table S1 (PCR primers) is named in the text.

a1_downloadable.note: All four processed files are public on the NCBI FTP site with no login; I downloaded three (77 KB, 2.4 MB, 908 KB). Raw reads are in SRA under PRJNA1203588 and were deliberately not fetched.

a2_label_is_a_column.note: For the binding project the measured label is a column: each of 3,360 peaks carries an enrichment/significance score, and a genome-wide log2 IP/input track exists. Caveat: the bound-versus-unbound framing needs a background set that is not in the files, and the paper's splicing label (5,070 rMATS events) was never deposited, so that version of the project would fail A2.

a3_inputs_present.note: The peak file gives hg38 coordinates only, so sequences require one bulk reference-genome download (~1 GB) and local extraction - a single lookup resource, not thousands of per-row queries. Gene tables carry Ensembl gene IDs plus symbols.

a4_units_stated.note: DESeq2 and count files have named columns in standard units (log2 fold change, adjusted p-value, raw read counts). The peak BED is headerless: column 4 (range 2-88) and column 5 (range 2.0-5.8) are most plausibly -log10 p-value and log2 IP/input enrichment from the methods text, but which is which is inferred, not documented.

a5_enough_rows.note: 3,360 peaks is above the ~400 floor for classification but far below ENCODE-scale per-protein peak sets used by published models. The gene table has 38,092 genes with a fold change, but all from a single 3-versus-3 contrast, so the number of independent experiments is one.

a6_fits_laptop.working_set: ~1.2 GB (hg38 reference ~1 GB plus 40 MB of deposited tables)
a6_fits_laptop.note: Everything downloaded is under 2.5 MB per file; the only large item is the reference genome, read per-chromosome. No GPU needed.

a7_counts_match_paper.note: Verified in the files: the paper's 3,452 differentially expressed genes, 1,317 down and 2,135 up, reproduce exactly from the deposited DESeq2 table at adjusted p < 0.05 and >2-fold. The paper never states a peak count, so the 3,360 peaks cannot be cross-checked.

a8_label_provenance.note: Labels trace to physical measurement: peaks come from CLIPper plus IDR on actual eCLIP reads with input normalisation, and fold changes come from DESeq2 on read counts. No column is another model's prediction. Peak calls are still pipeline output, so the positive set depends on CLIPper's thresholds.

B1.why: Two usable tables (peaks, gene fold changes); joining them needs hg38 coordinates plus gene annotation.

B2.why: All three gzipped files parsed first try with pandas; no fixing needed.

B3.why: One assay, one lab; peak scores already normalised by the authors as IP versus input.

B4.why: Peak score column floored at 2.0 (threshold truncation); 22,488 gene rows have no fold change.

B5.why: Verified: 0 duplicate peak coordinates, 60,580 unique gene identifiers in both tables.

B6.why: DESeq columns named and standard; the peak BED is headerless with no readme, column meanings inferred.

C1.why: Transfer question is informative either way, but with one protein and 3,360 peaks any answer is anecdotal.

C2.why: iDeepB (2025), RBPNet (2023), DeepRiPe, Multi-resBind, RBPsuite 2.0 are open; a 37-method benchmark exists.

C3.why: Diversity angle only: a non-canonical protein absent from ENCODE, in a non-ENCODE cell line, but n=1 protein.

C4.why: eCLIP is costly lab work, but for one protein the experiment was already done once here.

C5.why: Obvious dummies (shuffled or composition-matched background) plus published iDeepB/RBPNet numbers on comparable eCLIP data.

D1.why: RNA-FM, an open-weight RNA language model, matches short RNA sequence windows; DNABERT-2 also fits.

D2.why: About 10,000 windows of ~200 bases: embeddings cache once on CPU, then a linear head.

D3.why: RNA-FM code and weights are openly released (MIT per its GitHub repository, not re-verified here).

E1.why: Chromosome column present in the peak file, so a held-out-chromosome split is immediate.

E2.why: Verified: 23 chromosomes with 29-358 peaks each, enough groups to hold out.

E3.why: Dummy baselines computable: composition-matched background classifier, or mean peak score.

E4.why: Only 2 eCLIP replicates and the deposit holds merged IDR peaks only; per-site replicate agreement not recoverable.

E5.why: Paper names a purine-rich splicing-enhancer motif in 35% of peaks that a working model must recover.

E6.why: Label shuffling and feature ablation are trivially runnable on a 3,360-row table.

E7.why: No second ECD CLIP dataset exists anywhere; ENCODE's 150 proteins do not include ECD.

E8.why: I reproduced the paper's own 3,452/1,317/2,135 differential-expression counts exactly from the deposited table.

G1.why: Verified: hg38 coordinates with strand in the peak file, Ensembl gene IDs in both gene tables.

G2.why: ENCODE eCLIP peaks for ~150 proteins join on hg38 coordinates; the paper itself did a 149-protein overlap.

G3.why: Coordinate overlap is many-to-many (one peak hits several proteins and transcripts); needs a collapse rule.

G4.why: Co-binding question with U5 snRNP proteins is answerable but largely descriptive, and the paper already did the overlap.

H1.why: Peak file is positives only; the gene table does include all non-significant genes as background.

H2.why: One cell line (76NTERT mammary epithelial), one lab, one protein, human only, 2 replicates.

H3.why: The honest claim can be written in one sentence (see honest_claim_h3).

H4.why: Methods and cell line explicit, but the missing splicing-event table and headerless peak columns are undocumented.

I1.why: RNA-binding-protein and spliceosome labs (the authors' group at UNMC, the Yeo lab) but no clear user of an ECD predictor.

I2.why: Could at best reprioritise which transcripts to test for ECD-dependent splicing; the paper already names candidates.

I3.why: Precision among top-ranked sites matches the follow-up gel-shift experiment, roughly.

I4.why: HOMER already found the motif, so a k-mer logistic regression may match a deep model.

J1.why: Real splits and transfer learning, but much of the work is building a background set, not modelling.

J2.why: Splicing and motif biology is checkable; the published purine-rich motif gives a sanity anchor.

J3.why: Minimum shareable version is a tidy peak-plus-sequence table, which largely restates the paper.

J4.why: Scope would fit two weeks, but no budget is committed anywhere.

J5.why: No kill date or condition written down for this candidate.

existing_models.name: iDeepB (deep network predicting protein-RNA binding signal along transcripts, Nucleic Acids Research 2025)
existing_models.score_and_split: Pearson correlation 0.31 on full-length transcripts, signal area-under-curve 0.82, peak area-under-curve 0.68; split by chromosome (train on the rest, validate on chr2/9/16, test on chr1/8/15); trained on 225 eCLIP datasets covering 150 proteins in K562, HepG2 and adrenal gland.
existing_models.authors_named_unsolved: No evaluation on proteins absent from training; poor performance on less canonical binding sites; RNA structure and modifications not modelled; adding RNA-FM language-model embeddings did not help.

existing_models.name: RBPNet (sequence-to-signal model of CLIP crosslink counts, Genome Biology 2023)
existing_models.score_and_split: Reported average area-under-curve 0.89 across proteins versus 0.74 for DeepRiPe, on eCLIP, iCLIP and miCLIP data (split details not retrieved; the article page redirected and I did not refetch).

existing_models.name: DeepRiPe (multi-task convolutional network for in vivo RNA binding)
existing_models.score_and_split: Average area-under-curve 0.74 as reported by the RBPNet authors.
existing_models.authors_named_unsolved: Experimental bias and limited architecture capacity, per later papers.

existing_models.name: Multi-resBind (residual-network multi-label classifier, BMC Bioinformatics 2021)
existing_models.score_and_split: Improves on DeepRiPe in area-under-curve and average precision on CLIP data (exact numbers not retrieved).

existing_models.name: RBPsuite 2.0 (deep-learning binding-site prediction suite with web server, BMC Biology 2025)
existing_models.score_and_split: Suite covering many proteins and species; per-protein numbers not retrieved.
existing_models.authors_named_unsolved: Coverage of species and proteins without CLIP data.

existing_models.name: Horlacher et al. benchmark of 37 protein-RNA interaction methods (Briefings in Bioinformatics 2023)
existing_models.score_and_split: Benchmarked 11 representative methods across hundreds of CLIP datasets; establishes that negative-set choice drives reported performance.
existing_models.authors_named_unsolved: Comparability of evaluations and background-set design.

existing_models.name: DARTS and KATMAP (predicting splicing change from splicing-factor perturbation)
existing_models.score_and_split: DARTS trained on ENCODE shRNA depletion of 196 proteins in K562 and HepG2; KATMAP ships models pretrained on ENCODE splicing-factor knockdowns (numbers not retrieved).
existing_models.authors_named_unsolved: Generalisation to factors and cell types outside ENCODE.

backbone.name: RNA-FM (RNA language model) for peak-window sequences; DNABERT-2 as an alternative
backbone.hardware: Laptop CPU: ~10,000 windows of ~200 bases embedded once and cached
backbone.licence: Openly released (MIT per the RNA-FM GitHub repository; not re-verified in this evaluation)

integration.partner_dataset: ENCODE eCLIP peak sets for ~150 RNA-binding proteins (the paper itself compared against 149)
integration.join_key: hg38 genomic coordinates with strand (present in the peak file), and Ensembl gene IDs for the gene tables
integration.bigger_question_one_sentence: Is ECD's binding footprint just the shared footprint of the U5 small nuclear ribonucleoprotein machinery, or does it have sequence preferences no other profiled protein has?

controls.positive_control: The model must recover the purine-rich exonic splicing enhancer motif the paper reports in 35% of peaks, and must nail a trivially derivable target such as GC content from the same sequence windows.
controls.negative_control: Shuffle the bound/unbound labels and confirm collapse to the background baseline; also train on sequence composition alone to see how much of the signal is just composition.
controls.external_validation: None exists for ECD: no second ECD CLIP experiment has been published, and ENCODE's profiled proteins do not include ECD.

honest_claim_h3: A model here could only claim that it separates 3,360 CLIPper/IDR peak regions from composition-matched background sequence for one protein, in one immortalised human mammary epithelial cell line, from a single two-replicate eCLIP experiment.

plain_idea.one_liner: Use the sequence of a short RNA window to predict whether the protein ECD binds there.
plain_idea.train_on: Each example is a stretch of human RNA sequence (median 70 bases) taken from hg38 coordinates. Verified: 3,360 bound regions, plus an equal or larger background set that we would have to create ourselves.
plain_idea.predict: Output is bound versus not bound (or binding strength). The true answer comes from one enhanced CLIP experiment: the protein is crosslinked to RNA in cells, pulled down, sequenced, and enriched regions are called against an input control.
plain_idea.why_worthwhile: Labs studying the spliceosome would learn whether ECD has its own sequence preference or simply rides along with U5 small nuclear ribonucleoprotein partners; even a failure would show that 3,000 peaks from one experiment are too few to model a new RNA-binding protein.

more_or_better_data.why: 3,360 peaks for one protein in one cell line, against iDeepB's 225 eCLIP datasets covering 150 proteins in three cell lines. The only thing new is the protein identity and the 76NTERT cell line.

confidence_score.why: Only 2 eCLIP replicates, and the deposit contains merged IDR peaks rather than per-replicate calls, so per-site measurement noise cannot be estimated from the files I opened.

models_beatable.why: iDeepB is from 2025 with open code, a Zenodo archive and a held-out-chromosome split; RBPNet (2023) reports average area-under-curve 0.89. Neither is an old random-split model.

guaranteed_improvement.why: Fails the first condition: existing models are protein-specific and none was trained on ECD, so there is no published baseline predicting the same label on the same split that we could run and then extend.

ml_idea: Predict ECD binding along human RNAs from sequence: 3,360 IDR eCLIP peaks as positives, composition- and expression-matched background as negatives, RNA-FM embeddings plus a linear head, held-out-chromosome split, with the published purine-rich splicing-enhancer motif as the positive control. A second, weaker option is predicting ECD-dependent differential expression per gene from the deposited DESeq2 table, but that is a single 3-versus-3 contrast; the paper's splicing-event table (5,070 events) that would make the most interesting label was never deposited.

effort.compute_note: Estimated, not timed for the model: the three deposited files downloaded and parsed in seconds and total 3.5 MB; the cost is the hg38 reference download plus roughly 10,000 RNA-FM embeddings at a few sequences per second on CPU.
effort.cheapest_killing_check: Count the IDR peaks: it is 3,360 (already done, in the file). That alone is one to two orders of magnitude less labelled data than the per-protein sets that open models such as iDeepB and RBPNet already train on.

verdict_reason: The data is clean and genuinely verifiable - I reproduced the paper's 3,452 differentially expressed genes exactly - but Part C fails at 5/10: predicting RNA-binding-protein sites from eCLIP is a saturated field with open, honestly evaluated models (iDeepB 2025 with chromosome-held-out splits, RBPNet 2023, plus a 37-method benchmark), and this deposit offers only 3,360 peaks for one protein in one cell line from one lab, with no second ECD dataset for external validation. The paper's most interesting label, the 5,070 ECD-dependent splicing events, was never deposited, so that project would require reprocessing raw sequencing reads.
